about: Vectors for the x402/exact/aptos pairing: the aptos entry point of @integraledger/lcp. H is SHA-256("abc") from FIPS 180-2. The committed answer is Aptos mainnet transaction 0xde08191e…ef48ceb5 (version 7351075186) read over REST from api.mainnet.aptoslabs.com on 2026-09-25, trimmed to the members the reader returns. Fixture F's RawTransaction is built with @aptos-labs/ts-sdk 7.5.0 from that answer (max_gas_amount 15000, gas_unit_price 100, chain 1); its SHA-256 is Python's hashlib. idDigest is Python's hashlib.sha256 over json.dumps(sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':')) of the normal form. Other answers are the real one with the named member changed. The trimmed answer shows no events or changes: each committed answer here carries a Withdraw and a Deposit event of the fungible-asset framework and, at the deposit's store, an ObjectCore change naming its owner and a FungibleStore change naming its asset, in the REST API's shape; these, and every store address (SHA-256 of the owner and the asset), are constructed, and no node was read for them. The account answers (sequence number, ledger time and X-Aptos-Ledger-Oldest-Version) and the lookups' oldestVersion are constructed in the same way. The issue position given is version 7351070000. Each expected answer was derived by hand from read-status.md and the profile x402-exact-aptos.md. Ledger times are microseconds. A lookup by sequence number that finds nothing answers notFound with the ledger timestamp of that answer (the REST API's X-Aptos-Ledger-TimestampUsec header), so it shows absence only through that ledger. A committed answer is read only with its events and its changes, the members the read takes the deposits from: the same answer without either is out of the reader's form, unparseable, and never read as a transaction that deposited nothing (the profile x402-exact-aptos.md, rule 8). The rows that compare the signed gas members carry the real answer's max_gas_amount 15000 and gas_unit_price 100, as fixture F records them; the two 0x1::fungible_asset::transfer answers, whose arguments are stores, the answer with a script payload and the block_metadata_transaction a hint names are constructed in the same way. An absent transaction is unused only once the ledger time of the answer that read the account's sequence number (its X-Aptos-Ledger-TimestampUsec), in whole seconds, is at or past expiresAt: the Aptos prologue takes a transaction only while timestamp::now_seconds() < txn_expiration_time, and refuses it from that second with PROLOGUE_ETRANSACTION_EXPIRED (aptos-core e53447e0, aptos-move/framework/aptos-framework/sources/transaction_validation.move). The V4 rows give status's answer under the profile read-status at the one mark, committed, asked about the act payment unless a row's query says otherwise; positions are ledger versions. A transaction committed at the sequence number consumed it: one that is not the act asked about, its deposit reaching a store another account owns, signed by the payee, or an act the caller gave, answers failed instrument-consumed, and one with success false failed transaction-failed (the profile, rule 11). The account's number passed with nothing returned at it answers pending search-incomplete (read-status rule 23). Nothing at the number with the account not past it answers pending instrument-live before the expiry and failed instrument-unused from it; each of these is decided only where the history floor of every answer is at or below the issue position, and otherwise answers unreadable history-gap (read-status rule 18).

agreedRefusals.about: Refusal codes where the pairing leaves the code to the implementation. A transaction written {"$repeat": [s, n]} is s repeated n times; the rows below repeat AA and U+10000, four UTF-16 code units and three code points, and a length is counted in UTF-16 code units, as JavaScript's String length counts it.

buyer.about: The buyer gate's rows for this file's pairings, in the form of buyer.json's rows. B2 is the plant: the document advertises H, the hash of the ATR in B6's first check, and the link serves the planted ATR, that ATR with one byte changed; the gate declines hash-mismatch and never calls the signer. B6 is the pairing's bound check over the payment this file already holds: check(ATR, presented) gives H, and check(planted ATR, presented) declines signed-not-bound. Where the ATR is abc, H is its SHA-256 (FIPS 180-2 B.1) and the planted ATR is abd. SHA-256 values are GNU coreutils sha256sum, which openssl dgst -sha256 matches. Bytes are hex. A B2 input names the account, the buyer's inputs and the time (now, in seconds) its build needs. noSignedPayment names each pairing of the file that has no B6 row, and why.

noSignedPayment.x402/exact/aptos: The file records the transaction's fields; its signature is made by a key generated at each test run.

boundAccepted.case: The file's payment presented under options this pairing's read does not offer, each the payment's own option changed as the row's case names, or another pairing's option: bound holds the presented accepted to the option filter read applies and refuses each with the row's code, the code advertise gives that option (x402/option-not-this-pairing for an option that is not this pairing's). payment is a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into this file. This file holds no signed payment (buyer.noSignedPayment), so payment is the one here: the fixed option, the echoed legal context of H, and an empty transaction, which bound reads only as a string.
